data.title: Tokenized Stocks Will Be Crypto’s Next Big Wave w/ Andrew McCormick of Chainlink
data.transcript_raw: Welcome back to Real Vision Pro. I'm Ash Bennington. Time for a deep dive onto one of the hottest topics right now in the blockchain space. Of course, tokenization is what we're here to talk about today. Few crypto companies are at the heart of it quite as much as Chainlink. So, I'm happy to say we are joined today by Andrew McCormack, Head of Institutional at Chainlink Labs. Andrew, first time on Real Vision, welcome. >> Thanks so much, Ash. And thanks for everybody for watching. Happy to be here. >> Listen, this is a conversation I've been thinking about for some time here today. This is really interesting to me because this is really at the very heart of one of these sort of mega trends that we see right now in the digital asset space, which is the integration of blockchain technology with the TradFi space. You're someone who has a very strong background in traditional finance on the regulatory side, on the legal side. First, tell us a little bit about your journey into this space. >> Yeah, it's been an exciting journey. And sometimes I have a how did I end up here kind of moment to myself. So, I've been in finance since 2010. Started my career as a lawyer doing typical lawyer things, but try not to be too scary, too intense, too nerdy, any of that kind of stuff cuz I love innovation and helping make finance easier and more accessible for everybody. 2014, I have my first two kids. I have twins. My dad is coming to visit a lot, see his first grandkids, help out. He starts talking about two things all the time. One is pickleball. Two is Bitcoin. And I had no idea what he was talking about. I thought he was crazy. And sure enough, he was right on both of these trends. So, for a few years, he's always talking to me about Bitcoin. Look, I admit, I thought he was crazy. I was a skeptic. But then suddenly, 2016, 2017, it just clicked. And I realized this could be a better form of money, a better payment rail structure, a better financial system. So at the time I was sitting at E*TRADE as a lawyer and it was cool to learn as you're former E*TRADER as well and I put my hand up and said we got to do something in this space and everyone looked around and said we don't know what you're talking about. What does this mean? And so I went on a bit of a an adventure through E*TRADE talking about Bitcoin, blockchain, tokenization and what this could mean. And it was amazing to see the change. At first it was like we don't know what you're talking about to then this sounds kind of interesting to what can we do in this space and ultimately Morgan Stanley acquired E*TRADE and I joined the Morgan Stanley family, loved it but I wanted to just dive into the space even more so ended up going over to eToro where I was the US CEO and I loved it. It was a great experience but eToro spent probably half my time in blockchain and crypto and tokenization, the other half in traditional equities trading and options trading which look I love but I believe a place like Chainlink and where the blockchain technology is going is truly going to build a better world. So I wanted to spend every single minute of my work day doing those types of things. So it's actually 3 months today I joined Chainlink Labs and have loved every second of it. >> You know it's interesting. I probably was at E*TRADE briefly and certainly less gloriously and effectively I'm sure than you were but it was in the in those in those pre-acquisition days. It was very much a tech forward shop. It was really an interesting place to be for for that very reason, one of the reasons why I enjoyed being there. By the way I've enjoyed I've had the pleasure of interviewing Ayon the co-founder of eToro right here on this platform on Real Vision. But it's it's it's really interesting as we as we look at this moment where we are right now in 2026. I'm wondering if you could talk a little bit about the trajectory of where we were uh maybe just 5 years ago uh in the digital asset / cryptocurrency space because it's been a a massive shift uh in all of the things that you spend a great deal of your time focusing on, I imagine, uh which is the legal, regulatory compliance framework uh that really is the gateway uh for allowing some of these underlying technologies that you and I have been interested for such a long period of time into the regulated traditional finance space. I know this is something that you talk a lot about. Tell us your take on where we are at this moment and how we got here. >> It's actually happening, which sometimes I do a double take cuz it's hard to believe, especially when you think where we were 3, 4, 5 years ago, where it was scary to innovate and you felt like you couldn't do it or regulators, examiners, state attorney generals were going to come and throw you in regulatory jail, sue you, and we saw that happen time and time again. Look like any space, there's there's some shady characters, right? Every industry has them, and so some of that is well-intentioned, but it captured a lot of people doing a lot of good and making cool products that will truly help people, and that stifles innovation. And especially if you look at from the lens of a financial company, other than maybe aeronautics and medicine, there's probably not any industries that are as heavily regulated as finance. Which is a good thing because you're talking about people's hard-earned dollars, retirement accounts, so there should be a lot of regulations. But people are not going to build in a space when you don't know if it's going to be legal or not, if you're going to get sued or not, and especially at a large financial institution that's been around for decades, 100, 200-plus years, you're not going to take a chance on some, "Hey, this is the hot new trend. We don't know where this is going." So getting that temperature lowered has been critical, right? I think the crypto industry, blockchain industry, we don't need special favors, don't need government handouts and special like, you know, benefits and things like that. Just need a fair shot. And in recent years, we're not getting a fair shot in terms of like innovation. And that that changed with the change of the SEC, right? Where I think you're you saw a just 180 in terms of the speeches, the guidance, tone, the temperature to give people the confidence to start moving in this direction. And it's made a massive difference. It's a little over a year ago, even something more intense, but the genius act passed. And it's not a surprise since then we've seen just an increase in adoption of stable coins. We've seen banks plowing into the space. I think just last week, a consortium of 21 banks announced they're going to develop their own stable coin. That doesn't happen without the genius act. To the small credit union in Minnesota has existed where going to do our stable coin. And the example I love maybe the most is Western Union. It's hard to think of like a more old-school type of financial company. They're doing their own stable coin. And so, bringing that temperature down from a regulatory side, people stop suing suing folks, and getting actual legislation has made such a difference that will make a difference for many many years. >> Yeah, it's interesting. It really does seem as though uh stable coins were kind of the gateway drug for the uh regulatory framework that we saw, genius act obviously being a significant one. Uh clarity act still very much up in the air uh here today. You can go and take a look I guess on on Cal-She and see what the latest odds of that passing are. But it really has been just an extraordinary uh say uh 24 or so months uh for the digital assets spaces we as we have these conversations about the integration of traditional finance and the underlying blockchain technology. I'm I'm curious how you think about that broadly. Uh what do you see the role of blockchain technology, of cryptocurrency being uh in the traditional finance or maybe uh the better way to say it now in 2026 is the regulated financial space. >> I dig it. All right, that's a term I might use in in future discussions. Cuz that's exactly what this is. So, I think blockchain digital assets, it's not about let's burn down the current system, let's kick out all the old school folks. It's about making those existing rails better, faster, stronger, more automated, cuz it's a very complicated system built on very complicated laws some going back to the 1930s. And so, to me when you talk about whether stable coins or smart contracts or pro-program money, the fact that people can do stuff they do today, but just quicker, faster, less innovate intervention, think ironically lower risk, right? And increase opportunities. It's about making the rails better in my mind. >> Yeah. So, talk a little bit about that in terms of the implementation. What do you see? What's most interesting to you? And and and and describe what you see happening right now in 2026. We see those stories they're no longer just on CoinDesk, they're no longer just on Real Vision. Now, you read them now in the Wall Street Journal. >> Yeah, so I think two things that really stand out to me the most. This is after my my 3 months here, right? And I'm learning constantly and the two things that have really surprised me. One is traditional finances interest in DeFi. So, I cannot have imagined that in 2017 when I first started working in the space even two, three, four years ago. People in traditional finance knew of DeFi, but it was sounded scary and strange. And an example I sometimes use is a especially as a father of four and a kid of the '80s and '90s who loved The Lion King. There's a famous scene where Mufasa takes Simba to the top of Pride Rock and he says, "Everything the light touches is your kingdom except for this shadowy area over there." And that's kind of how a traditional finance looked at DeFi like, "I don't know what's going on over there. That's not our space." And since I've joined Chainlink, I realized that's not the case cuz people in traditional finance can see the benefits of a lot of liquidity, a lot of customers, a lot of innovation, right? And I love this idea of marrying both worlds together, the best of traditional finance, the risk, the governance, the innovation, alongside DeFi, just the technology, the quick moving, the liquidity. So, that's that one, that marriage of DeFi and TradFi I'm seeing, which is a surprising, but I think wonderful. And second, you know, we've seen a big explosion of stablecoins cuz I think there's true product market fit. There's a use case there. You have regulation there. To me, the next wave will be tokenized equities. And look, I will admit I am biased cuz that was my life for 15 years, equities trading. I loved it. I love it not just from the institutional side. I think everybody should open a broker's account and start making small investments to make a big difference in the long term. But I think tokenized equities are another one where there is a real use case, real product market fit. Right? Here we are on Tuesday after Labor Day. If you wanted to place a trade in your favorite stock for the last couple days, you really couldn't. You didn't have that option cuz the markets are closed. And if you are sitting in France or Singapore or somewhere else right now and you're wanting to trade and markets open four minutes, like you're at dinner, you're at work, and that's that's clunky. And I think tokenized equities can really open not just days of the week and hours of the day, but international markets in a new way. >> Yeah, I'm really I'm really curious about what that might look like. One of the most sort of fascinating developments to me over the last say 2 plus years has been this this this beginning to close of a chasm that existed, and it was a pretty significant one. I mean for for many years there there was TradFi and there was DeFi and never the twain shall meet. They were just two totally and completely separate universes. And now we see the beginnings of that with equities, but also for that matter with fixed income, currencies, commodities, the entire panoply of different asset classes having the potential to move into the blockchain decentralized space. It's really it's really an interesting moment. You mentioned one of the most obvious use cases there. And it's interesting because you of course see that places like Nasdaq pursuing these longer trading hours. It's been a trend that we've seen across markets well really my whole time working in financial markets the the gradual expansion of the hours of trading of ECNs, of figuring out how to bridge some of those gaps. So one of the most obvious there that you mentioned is this the quest for 24/7 access to US equity markets indeed global equity markets presumably at some point. But but talk a little bit about how you see that being implemented and what the role of the digital assets may play in that transition, the decentralized digital assets may play in that implementation in your view. >> Yeah, great question. So I don't think nice see Nasdaq or their similar exchanges are talking about 24/5, 24/6, 24/7 without blockchain. I think blockchain and digital assets and Bitcoin, that's what really got this party started. And I think it'll make it much more possible in the sense of if you can have trading embedded in smart contracts and somehow more programmatic and you're not relying on a central party, that is going to be much more accessible to 24/7 global trading because the reality is are if you are a US broker dealer today, there's rules on who you can serve around the world and if people are trading, you need someone in that operations team sitting there. You know, in middle of the night, you need someone from the customer service team serving all those people. So, some of those needs are I think less if you have smart contracts and more peer-to-peer type trading. And we're not going to get there tomorrow, right? And probably not even next year, but I think where this eventually goes and I think it's a really cool unlock is say Ash, you go about your day and you see some news about a company and you're like, that looks really cool and you know, we went out to lunch and I have stock in that company. Like, you buy it from me directly. Instead of going through a a party, an exchange and I think that's where this ultimately going. Getting there is complicated, but um I I really cool opportunity to unlock a lot of markets and my eToro experience showed me a lot on this point. As Americans, we like to think the whole world revolves around us and sometimes it does, sometimes it doesn't, but you've got tens of millions, hundreds of millions of investors who are not in the US, who are waking up at weird hours. But most of the time, they're wanting to invest in US equities. Giving that um customer class that opportunity to do so along their lines and trading hours, I think will be much more effective. >> Yeah, obviously the the deepest and most liquid capital markets and the deepest and most liquid equity markets in the world. Uh one does at least hope uh that it starts here in the the United States as a leader in the decentralized revolution uh as we have been in the in the traditional financial revolution and in and in the uh in that the uh the automated component of that. I mean, the United States, we're talking about E*TRADE, but lots of other innovators in the space uh for the for the for the web 1.0, web 2.0 technological revolution that we saw in finance. It really is an interesting moment to see uh where we might be in terms of the decentralized component of that revolution. I I'm curious, talk a little bit, I know you've just recently uh joined Chainlink, but you've obviously been thinking about these issues for a long time. Talk a little bit about how you envision Chainlink's role uh in the space. I think most people probably can throw out the word Oracle when they hear uh Chainlink, but I'm curious how you think in a little bit more detail uh about the role that Chainlink may play in that transition. >> Yeah, so Chainlink the the desire and what we're building is to build the infrastructure that connects DeFi to TradFi, right? Blockchains to the real world. Uh so, well beyond the world of Oracles, right? That's That's where we started many years ago, but from there we've grown significantly as the market has. One of my favorite authors in the space, he works for StockTwits, and he recently said, "Talking about Chainlink as a Oracle company is like talking about Amazon as a seller of books." Right? That's how you started, and we've grown from there. So, um data and making sure it's secure and accurate, empowering DeFi was our start. Since then, of course, we're doing the same thing in traditional finance and connecting the world together. Cross-chain is a big part of what we do, right? We believe we will live in a multi-chain world, and we are chain agnostic. So, whether it's ETH or Solana or Avalanche, and especially what I love is the thought of right now there's college freshman sitting in a dorm room coming up with ideas that probably be part of our system in the next couple years. And whether finance is using that future chain or one exists today, can use Chainlink to move cross-chain. Um especially as this space is getting more and more traditional finance heavy, thus regulation and laws, compliance tools is a big part of what we're doing. Orchestration is a big thing also, just because a lot of this is complicated. There's a lot of moving parts. So, we have the tool, the Chainlink runtime environment, where you can plug into all this in one spot and orchestrate all these beautiful things in one spot. Privacy is another thing we're doing. So, Oracles, that's that's where we started. It's a key pillar of what we do and we'll forever do, but we're certainly growing a lot from there. >> Hey Andrew, tell us a little bit more about those pillars, uh how you divide up the business and how you think about the role. >> Yeah, so I think you know, data certainly number one, right? The Oracle, we power about 70% of DeFi and we want to copy and paste that, do the same thing with traditional finance. So whether you're the biggest bank, the biggest asset manager, the brokerage, if you are wanting to plug into DeFi, into blockchain, you should be using Chainlink rails to do so. So data one, two, cross-chain, right? So you're wanting to move assets across chain, that is a that's second pillar our tool CCIP, cross-chain interoperability. A lot of letters, a lot of impact, seen a lot of growth in this space recently. Just in the last four or five months alone, we've had over 15 billion dollars of assets migrate over to the CCIP tool. >> Andrew, could you break break down what that what the use cases are in business terms, in terms of CCIP, and how it does this this cross-chain integration? >> Yeah, sure thing. So say you have an asset, I'll use an example of a recent one we announced, BitGo, right? Publicly traded company and OG in the digital asset space, um big fan of Bitcoin, obviously. Their founder was recently in the White House with our founder. So BitGo is a big name. They have Yes. Exactly. So Amazing. Well, I'm I'm overjoyed to join such good company and with you guys. That's awesome. So they have a product wrapped Bitcoin, WBTC. So it's not just buying in the Bitcoin and you hold it in your wallet, but you can move it to different smart contracts, use it in DeFi and loans. Um and so BitGo is selected, I think it was probably August, maybe July, just very recently, they've moved over to using Chainlink's CCIP tool. So, if you buy this asset and you have it in say your Ethereum wallet and you want to sell it or transfer it to Avalanche or some other chain or whatever may be, you use CCIP to do so. If you want to then use it in DeFi, you CCIP to get there. And it gives just additional use case to these very important assets. I am a huge fan of Bitcoin. It's how I got started. One of my biggest regrets in life is selling three Bitcoin many years ago. And I wish I still held those. So, I love the idea though if you have this asset and you believe in it and you think I want to hold this but in the interim, I would like to get some cash to use or some type of asset to pay for day-to-day expense, vacation, whatever may be, this BitGo product enables that to be possible and using CCIP to get it into DeFi and back and forth is a way to do so. And so, this is an area we are growing a lot in the last few months and I think more to come. And just cuz our our priority is always security um and trust and making sure that people are using our products like they that are going to work how it's intended to do so. >> Before you go, that was just the preview. The full conversation goes much deeper. What's really driving markets, where the risks are, and how the best investors are positioning. That's what we do at Real Vision.
